thread.document:
Group members: Devan Perkash, Rahul Bir, Ethan Stone, Micah Mok

Blue Team Website for Special Participation E

We built a website to make Special Participation E submissions usable at scale, rather than living in an archived Ed feed. Our goal was to turn these posts into something that students can actively study from and that staff can review efficiently.

Here’s how our site concretely adds value beyond Ed:

Lecture-aligned playlist view
Our "playlist" page organizes Special Participation E posts by lecture topic and week. For each lecture, it surfaces relevant student submissions (e.g. tools, visualizations, explanations tied to that topic). This lets someone studying a specific lecture immediately see how peers engaged with that material, rather than guessing search keywords or scrolling through weeks of posts.

Save posts to build a personal study guide
As students browse the site, they can save posts they find useful, and those saved posts show up directly in the playlist under the relevant lecture topics. This allows students to build a personalized study guide over the semester (e.g. “good optimizer visualizations” or “helpful transformer papers”) rather than re-searching the directory each time.

Fast browsing with Quick View
From the directory, users can open a “Quick View” panel for any post to skim its content without leaving the page. This makes it easy to rapidly scan many submissions, compare approaches, or review posts without opening dozens of tabs (as most of us in this class have likely experienced while studying!)—especially helpful given the number of submissions.

Strong search and filtering that’s always available
The directory supports full-text search across titles, student names, summaries, and tags, along with category filters (e.g. Exam Prep, Paper / Reading, Tools & Implementation). The search bar stays accessible even when scrolling deep into results, so refining queries is always quick.

Meaningful categorization based on how students actually contributed
Posts are grouped into a small set of high-signal categories (paper reviews, visualizations, tools, etc.). These reflect topic patterns in the submissions and help users quickly understand what kind of resource a post is before opening it.

Highlighted submissions
Some posts are explicitly highlighted (e.g. interactive demos, detailed tools, substantial writeups). This makes it easy to quickly find strong examples, while still keeping the full set of submissions visible.

Embedded PDFs and automatic artifact extraction
Links and attachments are automatically extracted from posts. PDFs are embedded directly in the post page with an "expand" option, so users can read them inline instead of opening new tabs. Students can quickly click the extracted links from posts without having to search within the posts manually. Direct download links are still available for quick access.

Similar contributions for contextual exploration
Each post page shows related submissions at the bottom of the page with overlapping topics or formats. This helps users explore alternative explanations, tools, or perspectives on the same concept, rather than searching manually.

Clean, intuitive UI designed for repeated use
The interface is intentionally minimal and clean, optimized for scanning, filtering, and revisiting content throughout the semester rather than just browsing once. Design decisions were made to optimize for efficient use. For instance, when a student searches for a keyword, the site will automatically highlight the matching keyword within all returned search results, facilitating faster content discovery.
